clue.text: Dread being not entirely legal

indicators.note: only part of the word for legal is wanted, so its opening letter is dropped

parts.note: something legal is lawful, permitted by law

explanation.surface: Someone's fear rests on a deal that is only partly within the law.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dread' looks like a noun but is the old adjective, as in 'a dread sight'.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective, dread means terrible or frightful, a close synonym.

clue.text: Jack gets key and freedom

parts.note: a jack (jack tar) is a sailor, abbreviated AB for able seaman
a key to a puzzle is its answer or solution

explanation.surface: A man called Jack is handed a key and walks out free.
explanation.walkthrough: Jack is a common crossword word for a sailor, AB being an able-bodied seaman.
explanation.definitionFit: Absolution is release from guilt or penalty, a kind of release or liberation.

clue.text: Period added to the end of a sentence

definitions.text: Period added to the end of a sentence

parts.words: Period added to the end of a sentence
parts.note: reads like extra prison time tacked on to a sentence, but describes the punctuation mark that closes one

explanation.surface: A convict's term of imprisonment gets extended.
explanation.walkthrough: Period is the American name for this punctuation mark; the surface suggests extra time served.
explanation.definitionFit: This dot, called a period in American usage, marks where a written sentence finishes.

clue.text: A fetching breed of dog

parts.note: fetching sounds like attractive, but means a retriever, a breed bred to fetch game

explanation.surface: Praise for a particularly good-looking type of dog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fetching' suggests charming; here it means bringing back shot birds.
explanation.definitionFit: This breed is a retriever, trained to carry back game to the hunter.

clue.text: Keep a supply of drugs in something in the kitchen?

parts.note: a shop that keeps goods available stocks them
pot is slang for cannabis

explanation.surface: Someone stashes narcotics inside a kitchen utensil.
explanation.definitionFit: A large pan for simmering broth sits on the cooker, so it is found where food is prepared.

clue.text: Secure top of foresail in rough sea

indicators.note: the foresail's top letter goes inside the jumbled letters
a rough sea is churned up, so its letters are stirred into a new order
in a down clue the top of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A sailor lashes down the upper part of a sail in heavy weather.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rough' turns SEA into SAE, and 'in' places F, from 'top of foresail', inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Secure and safe are synonyms, both meaning protected from danger.

clue.text: Show progress? Don't exaggerate!

definitions.meaning: to improve or develop, as a pupil comes on well
an exclamation of disbelief, like 'Get away!' or 'Pull the other one!'

explanation.surface: Someone asks about improvement and is told not to overstate it.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means advance, and as an exclamation it scoffs at an overstatement.

clue.text: It's still produced in Ireland, though illegally

definitions.text: It's still produced in Ireland, though illegally

parts.words: It's still produced in Ireland, though illegally
parts.note: still seems to mean 'even now' but is the apparatus for distilling spirits

explanation.surface: Something is supposedly still being made in Ireland against the law.
explanation.walkthrough: 'still' reads as 'even now', but it is the distilling apparatus.
explanation.definitionFit: This is Irish moonshine, a potato or grain spirit traditionally distilled illicitly at home.

clue.text: Part of the orchestra with an objection to raise

indicators.note: in a down clue raising a phrase lifts it so it reads from bottom to top

parts.note: an is the article a
a but is an objection, as in 'no ifs or buts'

explanation.surface: An orchestra member has a complaint to bring up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to raise' turns A BUT upwards in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: This large brass instrument belongs to the orchestra's brass section.

clue.text: Preserved meat makes sailor grumble

parts.note: an old salt is an experienced seaman
to beef is slang for to complain

explanation.surface: Ship's preserved rations give a seaman cause to moan.
explanation.definitionFit: This is brisket cured in brine, a traditional preserved meat, notably in Jewish delis.

clue.text: Insect with wings of short span

definitions.meaning: the mayfly genus, a winged insect that lives only a day as an adult
things that are short-lived or transient, like old tickets and posters

explanation.surface: A description of an insect whose wings are small.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short span' suggests a small wingspan but refers to a brief lifespan.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names the mayfly genus and also items meant to last only briefly.

clue.text: Companion in recreation put down floor covering in gym

indicators.note: the laying and the mat go inside the letters for gym

parts.note: PE, physical education, is school gym class
to lay is to put down
a mat covers part of a floor

explanation.surface: Someone sets out a floor mat in the gym for a fellow player.
explanation.definitionFit: A friend you play games with is a companion in leisure and fun.

clue.text: Foreign sailors find girl without transport

indicators.note: in its old sense without means outside, so the girl surrounds the transport

parts.note: a lass is a girl
a car is a form of transport

explanation.surface: Visiting seamen meet a young woman who has no vehicle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking' but means 'outside'. Lascars were sailors from India or South-East Asia.
explanation.definitionFit: Lascars were seamen from the Indian subcontinent employed on European ships.

clue.text: Mr O'Casey crashed in American plane

indicators.note: something crashed is wrecked, so these letters are smashed into a new order

explanation.surface: A man named O'Casey is in a plane crash in the US.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plane' seems to be an aircraft but is a tree.
explanation.definitionFit: In North America the plane tree is called a sycamore.

clue.text: Hankerings for last of daily bread

indicators.note: only the final letter of daily is taken

parts.note: bread is slang for money, here what one earns

explanation.surface: Longing for the final crust of the day's loaf.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bread' looks like food but is slang for money.
explanation.definitionFit: Hankerings and longings are synonyms for strong desires.

clue.text: Rocket engineer

parts.note: suggests a space scientist, but Rocket was the famous 1829 steam locomotive

explanation.surface: A specialist who builds spacecraft.
explanation.walkthrough: George and Robert Stephenson built the Rocket, an early British railway locomotive.
explanation.definitionFit: The Stephensons designed the Rocket steam engine that won the Rainhill Trials.

clue.text: Non-metrical form of the Emperor Waltz?

definitions.text: Non-metrical form of the Emperor Waltz?

parts.words: Non-metrical form of the Emperor Waltz?
parts.note: an emperor's dance, a measure being an old word for a dance, is also a unit outside the metric system

explanation.surface: A query about the rhythm of the Strauss waltz.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Non-metrical' suggests verse or music without metre; it means not metric, like pints and miles.
explanation.definitionFit: Units such as pints, inches and pounds are British imperial units, not metric ones.

clue.text: Remove a summary

definitions.meaning: to take out or extract something
a short précis at the head of a paper

explanation.surface: An instruction to cut out a brief synopsis.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb the word means extract; as a noun it is a brief outline of a paper.

clue.text: Legally only of minor importance

parts.note: minor suggests trivial, but legally a minor is a child, someone not yet adult

explanation.surface: A matter that the law treats as trivial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'minor' reads as 'small', but in law it means a person below adult age.
explanation.definitionFit: Being too young for a legal right means the law still classes you as a minor.

clue.text: She's very likely to have kids

definitions.text: She's very likely to have kids

parts.words: She's very likely to have kids
parts.note: kids suggests children, but young goats are also kids

explanation.surface: A remark about a woman who will probably start a family.
explanation.walkthrough: 'kids' are young goats, and nanny also suggests childcare.
explanation.definitionFit: A female goat gives birth to young goats, called kids.

clue.text: Such a sewer may produce hostility

definitions.meaning: a sewer here is a thing that sews, not a drain
... is ill feeling, as in a ... match

explanation.surface: A drain might cause bad feeling among the neighbours.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sewer' looks like a drain, but it is one who sews. A needle match is a bitterly fought contest.
explanation.definitionFit: A sewing tool stitches cloth, and needle also means antagonism between rivals.

clue.text: The old sign of those not quite gentlemen

parts.note: ye is an archaic spelling of the, as in 'Ye Olde Shoppe'
an omen is a sign of things to come

explanation.surface: An ancient emblem belonging to men below the gentry.
explanation.walkthrough: Yeomen were freeholding farmers ranking just below the gentry in old England.
explanation.definitionFit: Yeomen ranked just beneath the gentry in the English social order.

clue.text: Last, but not least

definitions.meaning: greatest or utmost, the opposite of least

explanation.surface: A twist on the phrase 'last but not least'.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both furthest or final and greatest in degree.

clue.text: These are irritating for sightseers, naturally

definitions.text: These are irritating for sightseers, naturally

parts.words: These are irritating for sightseers, naturally
parts.note: ugly sights annoy tourists, and literally the sightseers' own eyes may be sore

explanation.surface: Ugly buildings spoil things for tourists.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as eyes sore: what sightseers' eyes naturally become.
explanation.definitionFit: Ugly things that spoil a view are offensive to the eye, hence irritating to tourists.

clue.text: Heroic tale from 'The Pickwick Papers'

indicators.note: the answer is taken from within the run of letters of the book's title

explanation.surface: A story of heroism drawn from the Dickens novel.
explanation.definitionFit: An epic is a long narrative poem or story celebrating heroic deeds.

clue.text: Obstacle for horse after start of steeplechase

indicators.note: the horse is placed after that opening letter
only the opening letter of steeplechase is used

parts.note: a nag is an old or poor horse

explanation.surface: A fence trips a horse right at the beginning of a race.
explanation.definitionFit: A snag is a hitch or difficulty, an impediment to progress.

clue.text: Unfortunately, Don's away at the moment

indicators.note: an unlucky turn of events scrambles the letters of the phrase

explanation.surface: Sadly, a man called Don is not here right now.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases mean currently, in the present day.

clue.text: A number with preference for a charwoman's job

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
a leaning is an inclination or preference

explanation.surface: A figure combined with a liking seems to describe a cleaner's role.
explanation.walkthrough: A charwoman is a British term for a woman paid to clean homes or offices.
explanation.definitionFit: A cleaner's work is scrubbing and tidying, the core task of the role.

clue.text: Co-ordinate publicity material linked to a film, say

definitions.meaning: to link up or fit together, as plans that dovetail

definitions.text: publicity material linked to a film, say
definitions.meaning: merchandise or a book promoted alongside a film

explanation.surface: Organising promotional goods for a movie release.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means connect; as a noun it is a product marketed with a film.
